areas.name: Project — identity, privacy, deployments
areas.description: Rules the rclient repository and its hosted instances must respect.

rules.text: Documentation must describe what the project actually does today. A claim is not kept when the code contradicts it — an uncomfortable truth is documented, not hidden.
rules.action: The Phase 1 documentation truth pass is the first task of the phase; no feature work or promotion starts before it.

citations.location: Reply to the Phase 1 plan proposal

rules.current: Met for Phase 1: the password claim is now true (opt-in, off by default); audio and KI statuses agree across docs; no server IPs or keys in the docs; the README's demo line carries the degraded warning; tests/CI counts and commands match reality after the T11/T13 corrections.
rules.check: Grep README/docs for claims about stored data, features, checks and deployment, and verify each against code/config; run npm run lint/test in both packages and compare with what the docs state.

rules.text: The RustDesk password is only saved in the browser when the user opts in through a "Remember password" checkbox, which is off by default. Without the opt-in, the password is used for the session and not persisted.
rules.action: Add the opt-in checkbox to the connect form (task T10) and document the behaviour truthfully (task T1).
rules.current: Met: web/src/utils/passwordStorage.ts writes rclient_password only after a successful connection and only when the 'Remember password' box (off by default, rclient_remember_password) is ticked; unticking deletes it immediately; failed attempts persist nothing.
rules.check: Connect with the box unticked and reload: no rclient_password in localStorage. Tick it, connect successfully, reload: password restored. Cause a failure: nothing saved.

rules.text: rclient.linkzy.dev stays the owner's personal production deployment. The public demo runs on the Contabo VPS under its own subdomain, so visitors never reach the owner's private relay.
rules.action: Keep the production URL out of README quickstart as the demo; point the demo link at the new subdomain once it exists.

citations.excerpt: i will keep this as my personal producion deployment since i use it every day to connect to my computers, but we can create a new demo in the  Contabo VPS that i allowed you to access in the connections. we give it another subdomain

rules.current: Done: demo live at https://rclient-demo.linkzy.dev (own stack, tunnel and key on the Contabo VPS); repo homepage set to it; production rclient.linkzy.dev untouched and no longer advertised as the demo once README moves to the demo URL (T15). Open caveat: public relay hbbr ports were refused from that host, so real sessions may fail until a reachable relay is chosen.
rules.check: GitHub repo homepage and README demo link point at https://rclient-demo.linkzy.dev; https://rclient.linkzy.dev remains the owner's production instance and is not advertised as the demo.

rules.text: The repository keeps the name rustdesk-custom-web-client: the official RustDesk web client does not work well with self-hosted relays, and that is why this custom client exists.
rules.action: Do not rename the repository; explain the name and the reason in the README's "Why this exists" section.

citations.excerpt: Keep rustdesk-custom-web-client (there is an official client somewhere in the official rustdesk repo, but it does not work nicely, this is the reason i built this custom one)

rules.text: The README's hero visual is static screenshots until the Phase 2 fake RustDesk host exists; then it becomes a GIF/video recorded automatically with Playwright, so it can be regenerated on demand.
rules.action: T15 ships screenshots; T20 (blocked on Phase 2) replaces them with the recorded GIF.

rules.text: A change counts as done only when the project's own checks prove it: unit tests, typecheck, lint and build pass before it is called finished.
rules.action: Helpers verify with the project's check commands and report the exact commands and results; CI (T13) enforces the same checks on every pull request.

citations.excerpt: When completing a task, verify it by running the relevant unit test or manually tracing the logic.

rules.current: Met: gateway and web both pass lint, typecheck, tests (24 + 19) and build from a clean checkout, and CI enforces exactly that. commit 20a36d7 fixed the 4 react-hooks findings in web (no rule disabled); the CI run on main after it is the proof.
rules.check: Clean checkout: npm ci then npm run lint/typecheck/test/build in gateway/ and web/ (all exit 0), and the CI run on main shows both jobs green.

rules.text: When a check fails, it is reported as failing. Steps are not removed, skipped or softened to make CI look green.
rules.action: CI keeps the lint step in both packages; a red run is reported as red and fixed at the source.
